caption: Hebrews compares Jesus outside the city gate with sacrifices burned outside the camp. The connection is explicit, but it is typology rather than prediction.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did “outside the camp” predict Jesus? Leviticus says sacrificial remains were burned outside the camp. Jesus was crucified outside Jerusalem.
slides.body: Leviticus says sacrificial remains were burned outside the camp. Jesus was crucified outside Jerusalem.
slides.heading: Did “outside the camp” predict Jesus?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Lev 16:27: [They] must be taken outside the camp; and their hides, flesh, and dung must be burned up.
slides.body: [They] must be taken outside the camp; and their hides, flesh, and dung must be burned up.
slides.heading: Lev 16:27

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Heb 13:11–12, BSB: Although the high priest brings the blood of animals into the Holy Place as a sacrifice for sin, the bodies are burned outside the camp. And so Jesus also suffered outside the city gate, to sanctify the people by His own blood.
slides.body: Although the high priest brings the blood of animals into the Holy Place as a sacrifice for sin, the bodies are burned outside the camp. And so Jesus also suffered outside the city gate, to sanctify the people by His own blood.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Heb 13:11–12

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Hebrews makes the connection Hebrews directly compares the two scenes and says Jesus suffered outside the gate to make his people holy.
slides.body: Hebrews directly compares the two scenes and says Jesus suffered outside the gate to make his people holy.
slides.heading: Hebrews makes the connection

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But the details are different The animals were killed before their remains were removed. Jesus was taken outside alive. Hebrews creates a theological comparison, not a prediction hidden in Leviticus.
slides.body: The animals were killed before their remains were removed. Jesus was taken outside alive. Hebrews creates a theological comparison, not a prediction hidden in Leviticus.
slides.heading: But the details are different

title: Outside the camp
